As you are leaving the cave you hear a loud roar behind you.  It comes from where you found the small child.  As you attempt to determine the identity of the creatures you see a group of large trolls running in your direction on flapping feet.
The noise of this battle is sure to attract more trolls if there are any in the immediate area.
Nothing special seems to happen.
You notice nothing different.
You are unable to see any results.
Nothing happens.
What do you want to do?

You see several dozen dead orcs strewn about the cave.  Most of the bodies have been nibbled on somewhat by some creature that must be quiet large.  The cave continues off to the back.  You hear heavy breathing and the shuffling of great feet.
Do you wish to move to the back of the cave to investigate?

You discover that this cave is inhabited by a mated pair of trolls.  Though you have approached with the stealth of a clemidian devil cat, the trolls can smell you as if you had sacks of bacon strapped to your backs.  Trolls like bacon!!!

You discover what can only be described as a nest for lack of a better word.  The bodies of even more orcs are heaped in mounds about the cave.  Beasts such as trolls need to eat a lot.  Why so many look to be hardly touched is a mystery.
As you continue to look around for anything of interest you hear the wail of a baby troll coming from the west.

In this end of the cave is a very frightened young troll. The babe must have witnessed you killing its parents.  Its eyes bulge like saucers as it looks at you in total fear. Suddenly the babe begins to relax.  The fear subsides for an unknown reason.
Unknown, that is, until you look behind you.  The babe's brothers and sisters have stalked up on you.  They charge you in an attempt to revenge their fallen parents and save their baby brother.
During the melee the babe has disappeared.  The remainder of the cave has nothing of interest.
As you travel deeper into the cavern you find that the skeletal giant had a trio of rather nasty pets.
You see a group of cacodeamon warriors.  Do you wish to engage them in combat?

You spot a small cave in the side of the mountain.  When you proceed inside to investigate the source of a strong acrid odor you are confronted by the true ruler of the Spider Tower - a powerful spider queen.
As you are journey through a grove of oaks, large snakes drop from the branches.  They intend to make an easy meal of you.

The cave dead ends here.  Chained on the wall are the remains of a hill giant that has been partially devoured.  You are unable to tell if the body parts were consumed before being chained to the wall or if it simply fell prey to scavengers.
You emerge into the musty confines of a large cavern.  It would appear the hapless giant was to be milk and cookies for the beast resting here.  Resting that is, until now!
You stand toe-to-toe with a blue dragon.  It looks at you and clasps its bony hands.  "Mmmmmmmm, you have arrived just in time.  I grow ever so hungry.  Thank you kind people for your generosity."
Your skin prickles, and your hair stands completely on end as if you are rubbing your feet furiously on a bearskin rug while wearing wool socks.
There must be a powerful source of electrical energy nearby.
You find a sizable cache of wealth and a small sack with a group of 4 daggers.
You have found your way to the alley behind the combat arena.  You see a large shack in the distance that you had not seen before.

As you approach the shack, a man wearing a leather harness exits from the hut and approaches.  "What are you doing here?  This area is off limits."  He turns to go back inside when suddenly a huge creature bursts from the shack.

The creature bears the remains of shackles.  Blood-soaked chains, wrapped about its fists, create crude but effective weapons.  The man in the leather harness yells, "Look out!  It's loose!" In hot pursuit, several armed men storm out the door.
You discover a scroll inside the shack.  It contains orders that the corporal train the troll to fight in the arena.  Bad idea!
Holes have been ripped into the thatched roof of an abandoned shack.  Bloodstains on the floor bear witness that the former occupant suffered a violent death.
The creatures that caused the demise of the former occupant are now back searching for more food.
This spacious valley is inhabited by immense herds of giant boars.  Viewing you as a threat, a group of them attacks you.
Large piles of bones litter the cave's entrance to the south.
A small side cave leads to the lair of a group of Mush-Men.  They are less than pleased with your invasion.

A giant ant colony lives in the area.   Escorted by a few warriors, a stream of workers blocks your path.  Burdened under the remains of a large animal, they disappear into holes built into the cavern walls.  Do you attempt to pass this phalanx of death?
Fresh water is a rare find in the underworld.  When it is available, it's usually claimed and carefully guarded.
A small gnome mining detail worked here. Now, nothing but their bones litter the ground.  One skeletal hand holds a precious bauble.
This dead-end cavern is occupied by some unfriendly shantiles.
Large boulders careen downwards from a ridge above.  Those not fast enough to avoid the rocks are crushed beneath a hail of missiles.
The hail of boulders forces you to take up a defensive position.  Gnath seize the opportunity to close ranks and attack.
They carried little of value.  This was a perfect position for setting up an ambush.  Be careful of similar attacks in the future.

You round the corner. Someone yells at you from behind.  Spinning around, you come face-to-face with seven young men.  Huge cats accompany them, and they look like wizards' apprentices.  Fanning out, they begin to cast spells.

You approach the gates of a huge citadel.  A large group of Dogre guard the entrance.  Upon your arrival, they draw weapons and charge.
Now unguarded, you gain easy access to the fortress before you.
The stale underground air comes as a welcome relief compared to the stench emitted by the inhabitants of this foul place.
You are in a storage room.  With a minimum of effort, the door could easily be barricaded providing you with limited protection against roaming bands of Dogre.
The sturdy, massive door to this storage room has been viciously wrenched from its hinges.  The unidentifiable remains of its scattered contents rotted and withered away long ago.
In the corner, half a dozen large Dogre snooze with indolent abandon.  They are resplendently decked out with an impressive array of new weapons.  Do you wish to attack them?
One of the brutes owns a small leather pouch that contains an interesting item.
An impressive cache of wealth has been stored at one end of this room.   Appearances would suggest that these pillagers have been hoarding and adding to this treasure for quite some time.

Two gigantic Dogre stand guard.  One of them quickly jerks down on a heavy, braided rope.  Before you can engage the Dogre in battle, you must first handle a head-on confrontation against some of their voracious pets.
The clamor of weapons attracts attention. Just seconds too late, several of the Dogres' comrades burst into the room.  Incensed, they strike out furiously to avenge their comrades' recent deaths.

You discover several dead gnaths strapped to large racks.  Blood still drips from fresh wounds on several of the gnath's necks.  You suspect that your arrival brought immediate doom to these poor saps.

For their own twisted amusement, the Dogre had tortured the gnaths for information.  Upon hearing the clash of arms, they probably assumed that a rescue attempt was in progress and  abruptly killed the gnath in an all-out massacre.

A spacious room stretches before you.  The walls appear to be draped with  gauze, and the floor lies covered with an undisturbed, thick coating of dust.  For mysterious reasons, the Dogre have not dared to enter this area of the fortress.

Upon closer inspection, you realize that the gauze actually consists of several wispy forms billowing softly along the  room walls.  They do not appear to be attached.  They are hovering freely in midair.  Do you approach?
A manifestation takes the shape of a  ghostly human figure.  It is manacled against the wall by smoky, ethereal iron chains.  A shimmering blue energy curtain envelops the figure.

The prisoner begins to wail and moan.  The energy curtain shimmers intensely in an  attempt to block the ghost's powerful magic.  Your head begins to throb painfully.  You feel overwhelmed by a piercing migraine headache.
Deep in your mind you hear a silky smooth, beguiling voice.  "Free me!  Destroy these bonds!  I shall reward you with the greatest gift a mortal could ever dream of."
A small jet black vial sits at the foot of the energy barrier.  It emits a foul black mist that forms the shimmering energy curtain.  Do you smash the vial and set the ghostly apparition free?
Free after so many centuries of bondage,  the ghostly apparition begins to wail forcefully.  Stabbing pain shoots up your spine and throughout your mind.
Staggering about in pain, you are fallen upon by a host of ethereal beings intent on your destruction.  "Foolish mortals!  Now I shall give you your great gift-the eternal peace of death!"
Though you have defeated this group of beings, the bond that imprisoned others of their kind to this room has been destroyed.  Dozens of wispy forms flee from the room.

Soon, ghostly wailing and the agonizing growls of dead and dying Dogre fills the halls.  Within minutes, the carnage is over.  The ghosts have sated their appetite for life. They return to the nether regions from which they have so long been absent.

The corpses of over three dozen Dogre litter the ground.  Their armor protects nothing but frail bodies of dried, withered skin stretched over brittle bones.  Their flesh appears to have aged hundreds of years within a matter of minutes.
You enter a large hall.  An old Dogre in long flowing robes stands alone at the far end.  Her back is to the door and she is unaware of your presence.  Do you approach?

With difficulty, an aged Dogre mage awkwardly turns to eye your approach.  She stands hunched over and despondent.  When you're close, she speaks in broken common. "I expect you desire vengeance for your fallen comrades.  I'll not defend myself."

"I am too old to be a threat to you.  I look forward to being rid of my duties and ending this miserable life."  She rambles listlessly and reveals that the clan chief, lord of this castle, strongly despises and fears all magic.

This mage Bregwart, once renowned for healing, has been confined here for years by the clan chieftain to perform cruel experiments on captured humans and gnath to gain knowledge for war purposes.  Do you offer to help her kill the chieftain?

"Well then, don't waste more of my time.  No one cares about old Bregwart.  I expect many believe that I disappeared from sight and died long ago.  I might as well end it all."  Clapping her hands twice, she disappears in a flash of smoke and sulfur.

"Excellent!  I have long dreamt of the day where I could face Cragentooth and crush him.  Night and day, he is constantly  surrounded by many warriors.  With the aid of your strength, I will finally be able to unseat him from power."

Bregwart leads you to a cleverly hidden passage.  "This way leads to his private chambers.  Cragentooth believes that only he and his most trusted bodyguards are aware of its existence.  I discovered it several years ago."
"Have your blades drawn.  Be prepared with magic on your lips.  His warriors are quick of wit and blade.  Our advantage of surprise shall not last long.  He is located just west of here."

You descend the passageway to Cragentooth's quarters.  Bregwart steps on a false floor tile.  The ground beneath her collapses.  She plunges to a bloody death, her body ravaged by spikes. You leap the gap to face Cragentooth and his warriors.  To battle!
You enter a massive building.  It appears to be an endless maze of hallways and corridors.
You descend a flight of stairs and  face a long, colorless hallway.  The lifeless air is close and stifling.  Your heels kick up ancient dust.
You dead end at a set of primarily empty chambers.  Some warped spears and a set of rusty armor lay in an abandoned heap in the far left corner of this chamber.

You rummage about the old pile of armor and weapons and find one item of interest.  A large sack of barbed jacks.  As you rummage around, you stir up a thick cloud of dust and are overtaken by a severe sneezing fit.
A ghostly apparition now stands at the room's center.  Raising a smoky tendril-like arm in your direction, it speaks in the ancient fespian tongue. "Seek! Ye shall find only death here."

The figure disappears into the cracks of  the wall farthest away from you.  As soon as it fades from sight, the wall completely crumbles.  A small hidden chamber is revealed.  Intent on protecting their final resting place, undead guardians stream forth.

Old rotted bodies lay about the room like an army of broken rag dolls-a twitching arm, a disembodied head- scattered parts are all that remain of this ungodly army.  Before you can regain your full strength, yet another figure emerges from the alcove.
Unlike the others, this figure must stoop to enter the room.  It is a massive zombie heading up a multitude of lesser zombies.
Do you wish to investigate the alcove that the ghostly figure retreated to?
You search the dead and mangled bodies but discover nothing of interest.
If you were in search of treasure, you are sadly disappointed.  If you desired to meet the ghostly figure, you're in luck.

You enter a large storage room.  It contains few items of any real use.  However, you sense something so slight, it is barely perceptible.  A sense of evil seems to pervade this room.  You cannot deny it's presence, and you shiver uncontrollably.

You enter the town jail.  Six cells have been sectioned off.  Two of the local town drunks can be heard snoring loudly, sleeping off their regular overindulgence of merriment.  Low, restless growling emanates from the other cells.

At a table near the jail's entrance, a pair of burly guards play a rousing game of bloody knuckles.  One brusquely demands that you state your business.  Used to curiosity seekers, they readily grant you permission to ogle at the caged beast prisoners.

"Yah!  We got orders from Captain Richards to see that these varmints get transported to the gladiator games.  Well,   dragging them through the streets is just begging for trouble.  Me and Ramius don't ache to risk our lives.  These be nasty beasties."

The guards watch you closely and exchange covert looks.  One suggests casually, "Looks like you could use some extra coin.  Want to take on the job?"  Do you offer to take the beasts to the gladiator games in exchange for 100 Gold Zembulian Zelots?
"Fair enough.  We don't blame you.  It's not a job we're looking forward to.  Our pay barely makes the task worth the risk, but there are few good paying jobs around here to choose from."

"Praise the maker, we have a taker!   We'll fetch the critters right quick.  Don't want to give you time enough to change your mind!"  The guards round up three large beasts imprisoned by heavy manacles. Chains link all three beasts together.

They provide you with a map that shows  the location of the slave gladiator prison.  "Take them here.  You can give this note to Corporal Sampson.  He will be the one that pays you.  Good luck, but beware!  These beasts are not as dumb as they look!
As your head clears from the initial impact of the spell, you catch a glimpse of the cleric swiftly disappearing behind the  temple's fortified door.

You enter the slave prison.  A potbellied Corporal Sampson is slumped over a shaky table.  He's slept through the entire ordeal that just took place outside.  The smell of elderberry wine permeates his clothes.  You try to rouse him to collect your fee.

Sampson awakens with a jolt and sits up quickly.  An offensive stream of drool has slid across his left cheek.  Heavy bags underneath his eyes imply he hasn't slept well lately.  "What's this?  Can a man have no rest?" You promptly display your contract.

Sampson swiftly scans the contract with disbelief.  "I see that you have been promised the sum of 100 gold Zelots.  Well, there is not that many gold Zelots in all of Bywater!  You may be very brave, but you are also very gullible!"
"I can offer you a few silver for your trouble.  That is the best I can do."  He begins to search his belongings for a few paltry coins.  Suddenly, a nasty brawl breaks out between two of the beasts.

During the battle with the mad troll, one of the troll's hands had been severed.  One of your charges hungrily snatched it up to eat.  However, another beast greedily attempted to steal the tender morsel.  This attempt has provoked an all-out brawl.
Before you are able to get the situation under control, the beasts erupt explosively into a convulsing ball of fur and slashing claws.  You are immediately  pulled into the fray.
Corporal Sampson is badly wounded during the melee.  He asks you to take him to the village healers.

"Thank you, good people.  I didn't look forward to facing Father Yenovich.   Years ago, I ran off with his sister and ended up exposing her to the black sickness.  She died soon afterwards, and I returned to the city alone.  He's never forgiven me."

He thanks you and rewards you with a huge amount of coin.  "I bid you a well and safe journey." You feel awkward about this magnanimous offering.  You suspect that it is all he owns.  However, local customs dictate that it would be improper to refuse.
"Vipers!  You shall hang for this!  You yellow dogs have not seen the last of me!"
Never one to miss an opportunity, you snatch up one of the dead beast's claws and slash Sampson's throat.  His life blood  gushes out to drench the trampled grass.

In his last dying moments, he gazes up at you with eyes of pure hatred.  "You will regret this.  My dying image shall haunt your nightmares again and again.  I vow to avenge myself for the sake of my children, now forced to grow up fatherless."
With the death of the cleric, the magical enchantments that animates his mindless undead army fades.  Without the magic to sustain them, the corpses collapse to the ground.

You transport him to the village temple for healing.  A cleric is immediately summoned.  Upon seeing that the injured party is Sampson, his eyes narrow with recognition.  He demands, "Is this man a friend of yours?"  What is your reply?

"You have made a poor choice.  Though I may be a man of the cloth, I cannot condone this man's past actions.  Your decision to be friends of this fiend has condemned you all to suffering."  Before you can respond, he casts a spell upon you.

"You're wise not to associate with this man and his sordid past."  Two young priests are quickly appointed to carry Sampson off.  "Leave now!  Your business is done." He withdraws back into the temple.  There are sounds of the door being heavily barred.
Frenzied shouting suddenly breaks out.  A patrol of men rapidly approach your position.  "They're the ones!  They left Corporal Sampson to die like a wretched beast!  Seize them!"

You arrive at a temple dedicated to Sestuona, goddess of nature.  You will be permitted entry only if you are willing to pay an outrageous price for the temple's services.  Your presence here is opposed by a powerful enemy within the sect.

You enter the outer office of the city's head magistrate.  Her assistant at the front desk is drowning in paperwork.  He inquires about your business. "So, you seek adventure."  He informs the magistrate of your presence. "You may see her now."

You enter a spacious, well-organized office.  The city magistrate is an imposing woman dressed in rich velvet robes.  You state your desire for adventure.  She asks you a number of probing questions.  You detail your background and capabilities.

She informs you, "Some rather nasty business needs to be handled.  If you wish to contract with me, I can offer you a generous sum for your services.  There are a number of commissions to choose from."  She considers her case files thoughtfully.

"Ah!  This looks like a job that could fulfill your desire for adventure."  She hands you a file to look over.  "Read this thoroughly.  It details the assignment and your compensation.  If you find the terms acceptable, sign and date the final sheet."

Notorious Bindwart Bigbelly is wanted for the murder of Vladimir, a captain in the Royal Brigade.  You'll be rewarded in gold talons for his successful capture or if you can provide proof of his death by your hands.  Do you accept the commission?

"Excellent!  Bigbelly regularly frequents a grog and mead house known as "Newt's Landing".  It's located in the northeastern part of the city.  Careful! It's a rough hangout.  Report back here when you have successfully completed your assignment."
You enter a sleazy tavern known as "Newt's Landing".  The title suits this damp, dirty place.  Only a newt should want to hang out with his friends in such a dump.

In the back corner, near a large table piled high with roast mutton, a large Orc warrior pounds down a crock of mead.  He fits Bindwart Bigbelly's description.  A second Orc notices your unveiled interest and points it out to him.
Large armed Orc warriors crowd the tavern.  The boisterous din turns suddenly silent.  They all seem to be waiting for your next move.

No one attempts to stop you as you rush after Bigbelly in hot pursuit.  You approach the tavern's back door and come to an abrupt halt.  Bigbelly stands in front of you, his back to a large stack of barrels.  His gleaming sword is drawn.
From behind you, several heavily armed orcs approach.  Congratulations!  It appears that with just a minimum amount of forethought, you have managed to wedge yourself between a rock and a hard place.
The magistrate's assistant informs her of your success.  He's given authorization to pay you.  You sign a receipt, receive your gold talons, and are quickly ushered back into the magistrate's office.
The magistrate thanks you gracefully.  She is notably impressed by your achievement and hopes that you will consider taking on another commission.  You proceed to look over another file.

A rabid beast is wreaking havoc among the king's vast private gardens.  Two servants are dead.  One of the king's dear friends was attacked.  You will be rewarded handsomely if you destroy the beast.   Will you take this commission?
You are just about to enter the king's private gardens.  Someone has posted a message at the front gate.  "Closed until further notice.  Do not enter under any circumstances.  You have been warned!"

You enter the king's gardens and begin to stalk for signs of the rabid beast.  Several  plants have been uprooted or mutilated.  You hear something up ahead on your right.  There are indications that the beast may not be alone.  Do you wish to continue?

You're shocked.  A sudden thought races through your head.  "The magistrate better pay extra for this!"  There is not one beast.  Instead, circumstances require you to engage no less than six ferocious beasts at once.
Do you ask for more money because of the additional work you were required to perform in the king's gardens?  OR   Do you accept the original contract amount?
The magistrate sees to it that you are rewarded handsomely with a bonus.  "You have earned it, my brave friends.  Come back later.  I may be able to offer you something in the future."

"You fools!  Your instructions were to kill one pet beast that had been infected with rabies. Instead, you have killed all of the king's pets. The king is beside himself! You have made a mockery of our contract and deserve nothing.  Leave!"
"If you don't exit this office immediately,  I shall summon my guards and have you thrown into prison."  You beat a hasty retreat out the door.
"Hey!  No one is allowed beyond this point.  You will have to leave."  Guards escort you to a door outside the cell block.
You climb up a staircase.  This appears to be the surface level.
A drunk dwarf has passed out on a bed of dry straw.  All your attempts to wake him fail utterly.
Opening the door to this cell was not a wise decision.  Several large fungus creatures sense their chance at freedom.  They appear eager and willing to destroy you if it will enable their escape.

Your attempt at unlawful entry to the town jail brings guards running.  They draw steel as they approach. "Planning to break out those miserable dunderheads we caught snooping around the graveyard?  Well, consider a cell your new home!"
Except for a few boxes stacked in the corner, the cell is empty.  You discover that the boxes contain numerous pamphlets.  They all promise benefits to those who worship Vixies, the Spider Goddess.
You open the door from the outside without difficulty.

You enter an area that bustles with clerks and aides.  They carry out their work with a self-important air.  Some sit at tables scribbling furiously.  Others struggle with armfuls of official-looking documents and sealed scrolls.
The air has become bitterly cold.   However, a soft glow emanates from the back of the room.  You are drawn to its suggestive promise of warmth.

Drawn to the soft glow, you edge your way slowly towards the far wall.  You find that you're shivering uncontrollably now.  Without any warning, the door behind you suddenly slams shut.  An icy draft sprints down your back.
The mortar, which bonds the floor's stone blocks together, glows with an unnatural light.  Will someone volunteer to touch the floor?

A green ball of light shoots out from the floor. Stunned, your volunteer collapses in a daze. The ball explodes into particles across the floor. Your feet feel an electrical surge. It zips through your bodies, shocking you like lab rats in a metal cage.

Coursing across the floor from the room's outer walls, the electric bolts of energy converge at a centralized point. Light particles swirl and swell upward forming a nebulous humanoid shape. Pointing an amorphous limb in your direction, it casts a spell.

From deep within the ground, you hear a  rumbling.  The stone floor begins to shake unsteadily.  Large cracks begin to split the stone surface.  Suddenly, the floor erupts into rubble.  An army of huge insects boil up out of the floor.
The summoner of this plague of centipedes has disappeared from sight.

You pause and listen intently.  The sounds are muffled and repetitive.  You suspect that they are the sounds of shuffling feet.  A strong odor of rotting, decaying flesh assaults your nostrils.  There can only be one explanation.  Zombies must be nearby.
You stumble into a swarming hive of zombies.  Several of them must have been created quite recently.  The place is bursting at the seams and appears hardly able to accommodate such a large number.
An old, mummified corpse sits in a corner.  Its right arm has been ripped off just below the elbow, and rats have gnawed off its feet.

You find Cragentooth's cot.  The mattress is infested by maggots, fleas, and spiders.  Disgusted, you broaden your search.  The place crawls with loathsome critters.  These conditions are repulsive.  You quickly determine that nothing valuable is here.
You are overcome by a bout of dizziness.  For some inexplicable reason, your compass appears unable to provide you with an accurate reading.
Created out of solid bronze, an imposing nine foot tall idol stands just in front of you.  The idol is in the image of a Anti'id.  Do you wish to destroy it?
With the figure destroyed, a small passage is revealed.  It had been secretly hidden beneath the base of the figure.
You descend into a tunnel.  Several clawed footprints have been left in the sand.  You proceed cautiously.  This tunnel may be used quite regularly.

Apparently, Cragentooth worshipped a graven deity in private.  You wonder what his followers' reaction would have been had they been aware of Cragentooth's lack of devotion to their own god.  He probably would have literally been skinned alive.
The idol crashes to the floor and splits in two.  A stream of small, glittering gems pour out of the broken figure.

You are just about to slip through the secret door to Cragentooth's quarters, when a brilliant light bolts down from above.  It heavily impacts the ground behind you.  You turn your head.  An eight foot figure stares over your shoulder.

The being looks very much like the idol you just destroyed.  It raises a tentacled head and speaks to you telepathically.   "Puny mortals!  I have been sent to take revenge on the desecrators of Xycloxyio's holy sanctuary."
"I expect to enjoy devouring your minds as much as Xycloxyio will enjoy devouring your bodies.  Xycloxyio will be most pleased with your capture."

The magistrate listens with courtesy as you relate your tale of progress.  When you have finished, she responds simply, "I assure you that you will receive your reward as soon as you have successfully cleared out the beast."
The place is stock full of provisions.  With a minimum of effort, you could securely barricade the door using some of these heavy crates.  For awhile, this could serve as a temporary resting place.

The circular room contains walls which are entirely devoted to scenes of carnage.  There are numerous depictions of large creatures with tentacled heads.  They're often shown attaching these tentacles to helpless victims' skulls.

Dwarves, elves, ogres, orcs and even  gnomes are shown having their brains extracted by the strange creatures.   Humans are depicted in only one scene. It's possible that the scenes are   chronological pictographs representing this race's history.

Humans are a young race, and they do not appear until the last scene.  Here,   humans are shown engaged in battle with the strange creatures.  The humans are fighting the creatures using highly developed mental capabilities, and they are winning.

Perhaps, Realmz owes its existence to the human race.  These numerous strange creatures were in the process of destroying all other races until humans appeared.  Somehow, humans were able to develop their psychic abilities to defeat them on their level.
Many ancient songs and stories have proclaimed that the gods created the human race to ensure the survival of the elder races.

After the devastating threat to the elder races had been eliminated, the gods supposedly lost interest in humankind.  The race had fulfilled its original purpose.  It was physically weak and unintelligent.  They agreed that it would probably die out.

However, one goddess did take pity on the puny race.  She granted humans the power to learn and the ability to work together.  While preoccupied over these ancient myths, you utterly fail to notice the arrival of several strange, tentacled beings.

There's no doubt that these creatures could have virtually destroyed Realmz and its inhabitants.  Their tentacles try to attach as you strain your sword skills to the limits.  Although you manage to defeat them, you shrink at the mere thought of an army.
Those that inhabit the Realmz are fortunate that these horrendous creatures no longer exist in such vast numbers.

As soon as you step into the hidden passage, you are assaulted by a mental attack.  It is a psychic barrier used to prevent weak-minded Dogre from entering this area of the fortress.  Your magical energy drains from your body.

You come across a large tentacled creature.  It is slowly dissecting a live Dogre, carefully removing and labeling various body parts.  Still conscious, the Dogre is unable to shriek or move.  It is gagged and immobilized by large leather straps.

You enter a large room filled with several unfamiliar objects.  Curious, you begin to experiment with several of the devices attempting to figure out what they're used for.  Suddenly, four creatures converge upon your party from opposite directions.
The Mush Men fight for their lives.  They have become completely surrounded.

You greet a passing wizard who smiles warmly at you.  You strike up a wonderful conversation and become friends.  He asks about your travels and would like to know if he may accompany you on your exploits?
You return to his small shack to gather his things before you set off with your new found friend.  His name is Vodalian and he states that he simply loves adventure.

A seedy looking group of gnomes are sitting at a vomit stained table.  They are swilling cheap grog from a clay jug.  They seem more concerned with getting more than their share of the wine and pay you little attention.
Just as you're about to dismiss the group,  Vodalian rears up a glinting dagger and charges against one of the gnomes.  "Murderous scum!  I shall avenge my sweet Alex this very day!"
You burst forth in an attempt to restrain Vodalian.   Gnomes rush from the shadows to aid their drunken friends.

Vodalian thanks you for your aid.  "This vermin slew my son.  Alex was an extremely intelligent and talented pupil.  He could have grown to become a powerful mage.  This foul creature deserved a more cruel demise."
The goblins scatter.  The body of their chief lies broken and still.  Blood gurgles forth amid the lonely quiet.
A large group of flesh fiends stand on the far side of the small stream.  They seem reluctant to approach the water.  If you venture across, they will surely attack.
Upon the destruction of the mush mound, the surrounding podlings wither and die.

You plow through thick clumps of fungus. Movement flashes at your side.  You halt and warily eye the surroundings.  A constant, steady rustling seems to come from all directions.  You feel quite on edge.  There's something odd about these plants.
Huge fungus-like plants grow throughout the area.  Each fungus is surrounded by small podlings attached by long vines.  The podlings slither in your direction.

A faint smell begins to permeate the air. It slowly gains strength.  You toy with the idea of capturing one of the creatures.  A wizard would pay dearly to use such a  plant in experiments.  The nasty odor hastily devours this thought.

Open grassland is marred by a dark, gaping pit.  Muted bubbling fizzles below.  A large log lies near the pit's edge.  It might be possible to use it as a crude, makeshift ladder.  Do you push the log in and attempt to enter the pit?

The cleric emits a low, guttural chant.  Near the cavern wall, corpses twitch and writhe.  Compelled to serve as  reinforcements to the cleric's unholy army, the grotesque bodies awkwardly disentangle themselves.

You start to slowly clamber down the log.  With a heavy thump, the log shifts to the right and begins to shake with violent force.  Clinging for dear life, you scramble your way back up out of the pit.  Massive slime creatures slither up the log.
Your movements attract the attention of another mush mound.
The clamor of battle attracts the attention of several krise.  They rush to the aid of their clansmen.
Several warriors from the village rush to defend their chief.
Several krise arrive on the scene.  The sounds of battle reverberating throughout the caverns have brought them running to investigate the commotion.
With the annihilation of Rewop, his companions are no longer able to remain in the Realmz.  They quickly fade away, returning to the smoky Abyss of their true home.
Rewop summons a minor demon to fight at his side.  He is an intimidating, powerful foe.
Fire fiends attack.  Their yellow fangs ooze steaming ichor as they lunge from every direction.

Deep crags and pits of sulfurous lava make the footing treacherous.  Periodically, growls belch from the hot inner recesses.  It's difficult to believe that some creature could breathe and survive these steamy, molten pits.
More centipedes boil up from beneath the floor tiles.  Without a pause, they crunch over the dead husks of their own kind in their relentless pursuit of you.
The Widow of the Web possesses the ability to control lesser arachnids.  She draws on this power to compel her lesser cousins to aid her in battle.
At the death of their leader, troopers begin to scatter and run.  You repeatedly bellow out orders for them to stand their ground.  The situation deteriorates into panic and disorder.
You walk down a dimly lit passage.  The odor of cheap wine intermingles with   spiced potatoes.  The raucous din of drunken patrons swells the close, musty hallway.
A worn carpet has been stained by  countless mugs of spilled ale.  Patches of mold grow in dark corners of the room.  The rotting remains of potatoes have been ground into the carpeting.

You head towards Bigbelly.  An Orc warrior steps forward and offers to buy you a drink.  The moment your attention is diverted, Bigbelly bolts for the bar's back door.  At this second, the path of pursuit is free and clear.  Do you dash after him?
You enter the musty, dank cellar.  Immense, dirty claw prints trail off into the distance.  From somewhere up ahead, growls rumble in a low-toned threat.
Encouraged by countless mugs of ale, a few of Bigbelly's buddies rise to attack.
It's pretty dark down here.  You may want to cast some light.  Click the TORCH button  OR   Cast a light spell if you have one.    -The Protector-
Several inches of rancid water cover the floor.  A cruddy drain is clogged by accumulated filth and grime.

You pry the warped trap door up by a huge iron ring.  The rusty hinges groan in protest.  Beneath the door is a small pit that holds a large leather sack.  The bottom of the sack has rotted away, but the contents are as valuable as ever.

A large pit slowly drains the stagnant water from this room.  In the bottom of the pit you see a large green pool.  It quivers as each drop of water hits it's surface.  Do you throw an object in the well to test it's depth?

You kick a large stone into the well.  It does not land with the expected splash.  Instead, it hits the green pool with a loud slap.  It sounds as if the stone has hit a large blob of clay.  If only that was the case...
A old ladder leads down a small pit.  You enter the small hole only to emerge into a small room.
A loud growl to the west alerts you that you are not alone.  With luck, this is knowledge the creature who made the growl does not have.
A number of flasks are in a crate near a barrel.  The barrel is full of lamp oil.  It's an easy task to fill the flasks with oil.
The rations in this sack seem fit for consumption.  They appear to be pilfered from the tavern above.  Obviously, the minotaurs must sneak to the surface and steal them.
Suddenly the floor gives way.  A large pit opens beneath your feet.  Those that do not DETECT TRAP do not see the danger in time and fall in.
The noise of the trap attracts the creatures that lives here.  As you manage to gather yourself together a pair of large minotaur rushes you from the west.
The foot locker is locked but it's easily defeated.
A large lever sticks from a pillar.  Do you move the lever?
The lava begins to drain from the pool.  It seeps into what must be an underground storage tank.
The pool of water drains through a drain in the wall.  It must be headed for an underground storage chamber.

The minotaurs must have used the lava for heat and the cool water to drink.  However, with both the lava and water in the storage tank below, a great gush of steam fills the room.  You are literally cooking alive.
With both levers thrown, you feel a low rumble below ground.  In now dawns on you that fire and water don't mix.
You throw the switch.  A loud bang sounds from nearby.

Several dead and mutilated bodies are scattered about the area.  Most look to have been slain patrons of the seedy bar above.  A few carrion slugs are cleansing the area of all dead flesh.  Your living flesh will be a welcome treat.
The room is filled with many provisions.  All of which are now rotten and useless.
Many tables and chairs are stacked in the corner.  At one time they must have been of some worth, but they have been rotting here for so long they are now worthless.

An old sump near the back of the room must lead to some underground cavern.  A few denizens of the deep have found their way to this room.  They are feasting on the sacks of rotting wheat in the corner of the room.
This lever is rusted so bad it will not budge.
This lever looks to have been oiled recently.  Do you wish to throw it and see what happens?
There are several potions of worth on this table.
You spot a group of the vermin that infest this decrepit cellar.  Do you wish to attack them?

As you eye a stairwell that leads to the root cellar, a nearby scullery maid speaks to you.  "I would not go down there.  Quite a few that do never come back up.  Olif has abandoned that cellar long ago.  Something's down there.
Olif has offered a generous reward of gold to anybody who can root it out.  So far none of the takers have returned."  Do you wish to enter the abandoned root cellar?
Olif, the owner of this sleaze pit rushes up to you.  Having heard the noise from below he speaks out, "I don't believe what I'm seeing  Thought for sure that whatever was down there had got you too.

I suppose your wanting to collect the reward I have out for the killing of what was down there.  I tell you what.  How about I give you a choice.  I can give you the gold, or I can give you what I have in my pocket.  What do you say?"

"If that is your choice."  Olif hands you a heavy bag of coin.  Olif pulls out his hand and reveals a ring with a large glowing gem.  He plays with it absentmindedly.  Do you ask him to reconsider and ask for what he has in his pocket?
Olif ponders for a moment and then nods.  "Very well, since you are so sure of yourself, you can indeed have what I have in my pocket."
Olif reaches in his pocket and pulls out a bright copper tarsk.  He flips it at your feet and walks away, "Don't spend it all in one place!"

He grudgingly hands you the sack of coins.  "If I were you, I would be moving on.  Quite a few in this fine establishment would not mind slitting your throat for that coin.  Now be gone before I have you thrown out!"

A pack of ghouls is devouring a man in the corner.  From the blood stained remnants of his cloak, he appeared to be one of the town guards.  With a sneer on their blood stained lips, they attack like a pack of wild dogs.
The remains of the man are scattered about the room.  He appears to have been a fine warrior in his day for he possessed a keen edged weapon.
Many mangled corpses and gnawed bones are heaped in the corner of the room.  A macabre site if you ever saw one.
As you prepare to leave the dead in peace, you notice one pile of bodies seems to shift.  From beneath the pile of bodies you can hear a grunting noise.  Do you investigate?
As you pull several bodies from the pile it begins to topple.  As the grotesque and misshapen forms slide from the pile you uncover several carrion feeders.
As you wipe the gore from your blades you spot a small ledger near the back of the room.  To read the ledger, select "Ledger" from the Maps/Notes Menu.
From somewhere behind you, near where you came in, you hear what sounds like a high pitched moaning.  The hair on the back of your neck begins to stand as you contemplate the source.
You see a trap door in the floor.  Below is a smooth sloping shaft.  Do you wish to slide down?
Do you push the lever?
A grimy drain, and a way to move about.
Many apprentice wizards are about the drudgery of taking inventory of their food stores.  Each apprentice will strive his best to prove themselves to their master by being the first to slay you.
You have found the animal pen.  The beasts within do not recognize you as their masters and attack before you can close the door behind you.
The very orderly quarters of the apprentices stands before you.  Most of those that call this home are gone.  However, a few are completing some studies.  They are quick to respond to your intrusion.

You enter the semi private quarters of the headmaster.  On a small table near the bed you see his daily diary.  The instructions on the cover are for the headmaster to fill out a daily report on the training of his students.
Each day that page must be ripped out and delivered to the grand wizard by the student who has performed poorly for that day.  Today's log is only partially filled in.
A gruesome site indeed.  The remains of some sacrificed individual lies heaped in the corner to rot.  A loud buzzing comes from the corpse as a plague of pests and zephyr flies feed on the corpse.
Two identical statues are in each corner of the room.  However, the statue on the right seems to have a soft white glow.
Inscribed in stone at the base of the statue are the instructions for a sacrificial ritual.  The eerie glow about the statue almost gives you the impression that it's alive.  In fact it's undead.
The noise has alerted a nearby Dogre patrol.

You approach the headmaster who waits patiently for your arrival.  A dead apprentice lies at his feet like a rag doll.  His body and face charred like overdone ribs.  He answers your question before you can even ask.

"I am not a believer in the old saying,  'Don't punish the messenger'.  If he had done his job, there would have been only good news to report."  With that said he seats himself in his fine silk chair.

"So you have slain my master.  No matter.  It only saves me the time of having to destroy that feeble man myself.  For many months now I have planned to overthrow him.  You only rob me of the pleasure that would have given me.

My enemy is dead, but you shall substitute in his place."  With lightning quick reflexes, he smashes a pair of amber crystals at his feet.  As you clear the smoke from your eyes you stair at the a pair of immense beings.

You find the secret treasure of the headmaster.  He has been massing his wealth and fortune for some time in anticipation of overthrowing his master.  This money would have gone a long way towards bribing the apprentices.

Though you have set me back with your wanton destruction of my students, I fear that battling you can only further weaken my position.  If you leave my quarters in peace I shall let you live.  Otherwise I shall deal with you harshly.  Do you leave?
You are very unceremoniously dumped on the floor like sack of wheat.  Your pride is not the only thing bruised this day.
You unwise decision to pull the lever has not only caused you to suffer searing pain, but has attracted the attention of a nearby group of apprentices.
This room is empty save a strong smell of perfume.
You interrupt a woman.  "Get out!  I shall have the town guard throw you in prison for this!"  You narrowly dodge a vase that is thrown at you.
You walk in as a rather embarrassed man finishes buttoning up his robe.  He mills about gathering his things and leaves in a hurry.
A storeroom.  Nothing of interest as far as you can see.  You could rest in here without being found.
A gnome is surprised by your boldness.  "I will ask you to leave.  I have friends in the town militia.  It would be best if I did not have to give them your names."  Do you leave?
Having called his bluff, he gives you a stern look and stomps out of the room.  "You shall regret your hasty decision!"

Waiting for you at the bottom of the stairs is the small gnome you so rudely interrupted upstairs.  Behind him is a large group of armed militia.  "That's them Boron!  That group right there.  Now if you want your gold, you will have to earn it."

As you clean your blades on the tunics of the fallen, you hear one of the employees of this establishment yell out the door to a group of nearby town militia.  She is calling for help.  You hear the clank of weapons and armor as they come running.
You hear the same woman call to yet another group.  However, they are far off and this gives you ample time to scram.
A burley dwarven warrior is snoring loudly on the bunk.  Several empty flagons of ale are scattered about the room.  Do you wake him?

He awakes with a start.  As he shakes the cobwebs from his head he begins to pat his belt.  Suddenly he stands and begins to shout, "Hey!  Who stole me purse!" Without hesitation he grabs a nearby ax and begins to swing.
"Me be tinkin me be knowing who has me purse!  Me be tinkin on getting it back, just quick."

Suddenly Reppep Rd stops attacking. "Oie!  Me be sorry folks. I guess I lost me head.  Twas the girl who me thinks took me coin.  Perhaps you will let me travel with you for a while. Tis a dangerous place to be traveling alone. Tink I tag along with ye."
"Oie!  Tis a good ting you be doing.  Me name is 'Reppep Rd'  Me been waiting in Bywater fer tree days for me mate to show.   Lookin be he not be showin."
